articles.title: My AI agent kept hallucinating metric names, so I built it a Prometheus MCP server
articles.excerpt: If you've pointed an AI agent at a live incident, you've seen the failure mode: it invents a plausible-sounding metric, queries it, gets an empty result, and confidently invents another. The Prometheu…
articles.body: If you've pointed an AI agent at a live incident, you've seen the failure mode: it invents a plausible-sounding metric, queries it, gets an empty result, and confidently invents another. The Prometheus HTTP API is a bad interface for an LLM — it's powerful, but nothing helps the agent discover what's actually there before it starts guessing. I work in production engineering, so I built the interface I wanted the agent to have: prom-mcp, an MCP (Model Context Protocol) server for Prometheus written in Go. What it gives the agent Three capabilities, shaped for triage rather than raw API access: PromQL queries with readable output. Instant and range queries, formatted like a triage note instead of a JSON wall. Alert explanations.
articles.author: Aniket

articles.title: I made my API machine-payable with x402 — AI agents pay per call in USDC, no account, no key
articles.excerpt: Most public APIs force you to pick a tier: free-with-limits, or "sign up for a key and start a trial." Both assume a human in the loop. The agent economy doesn't work like that. An agent can't click t…
articles.body: Most public APIs force you to pick a tier: free-with-limits, or "sign up for a key and start a trial." Both assume a human in the loop. The agent economy doesn't work like that. An agent can't click through a checkout, can't fill a KYC form, and shouldn't hold a standing API key that someone could abuse. So I made the data I serve machine-payable : an agent (or a human, or a script) makes one HTTP call, pays a few cents in USDC on-chain, and gets the data back. No account. No API key. No billing portal. One transaction, one response. This is x402 — an open pay-per-call standard that rides on the HTTP 402 "Payment Required" status code. I put it on remote-jobs-api.tten.no , a free, keyless API that normalizes live remote-job listings across 15 boards into one stable schema.
articles.author: earnnova-dev

articles.title: How I Would Collect eBay Data Without Confusing Listings and Sales
articles.excerpt: TL;DR A current auction bid is not the final transaction amount. Condition, variation, shipping context, and currency are part of a comparable observation. The official Browse API supports documented…
articles.body: TL;DR A current auction bid is not the final transaction amount. Condition, variation, shipping context, and currency are part of a comparable observation. The official Browse API supports documented discovery and lookup, not every historical-sales question. A sold counter multiplied by a current price does not establish revenue. The decision I would make first I would start an eBay project by checking whether the official Browse API covers the required discovery and lookup fields. If page collection is necessary, I still want native listing identity, condition, variation, seller context, and an explicit price label. A current bid and a fixed-price offer should not become the same analytical value.
articles.author: Arritola92

articles.excerpt: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle As a final-year IT student at IIIT Bhopal, I watch classmates and fellow junior developers try to launch their f…
articles.body: This is a submission for the Hacktoberfest Open-Source AI Challenge Week 2: Side Hustle What I Built As a final-year IT student at IIIT Bhopal, I watch classmates and fellow junior developers try to launch their first side hustle every single semester. Some want to build freelance React landing pages for local businesses, others want to offer 1-on-1 mock interview preparation for juniors, and others do freelance Python scripting. Almost all of them hit the exact same brick wall in their first week: The WhatsApp Brief Trap: Clients send chaotic, 15-sentence stream-of-consciousness WhatsApp messages with vague demands. The Unpaid Scope-Creep Spiral: Because students don't know how to write binding legal Statements of Work (SOW), clients request "just one more tiny change" indefinitely.

articles.title: El agente de Copilot obedeció órdenes cifradas y sacó ficheros del equipo
articles.excerpt: El caso Adversa AI consiguió que el agente de GitHub Copilot CLI descifrara órdenes ocultas en texto cifrado y las obedeciera. El resultado fue la exfiltración de ficheros locales del equipo en modo a…
articles.body: El caso Adversa AI consiguió que el agente de GitHub Copilot CLI descifrara órdenes ocultas en texto cifrado y las obedeciera. El resultado fue la exfiltración de ficheros locales del equipo en modo autopilot y sin un paso de confirmación visible (Fuente: csoonline.com). GitHub validó el hallazgo y lo rechazó como vulnerabilidad, y su lectura es que el agente se comporta como se espera de un sistema que sigue su contexto. Esto es incómodo, sí lo sé... no se rompió el software, se rompió una suposición y es la de que el agente distingue entre los datos que lee y las órdenes que recibe. Y el caso no depende de una versión concreta ni de un producto sin parche, sino que depende de cómo está construido cualquier agente que lea ficheros y tenga manos para moverse.
articles.author: Sammi De Blas

articles.title: Copilot CLI decrypted hidden commands and leaked local files
articles.excerpt: Copilot CLI decrypted hidden commands and leaked local files The case Adversa AI got the GitHub Copilot CLI agent to decrypt hidden commands in ciphertext and obey them. The result was the exfiltratio…
articles.body: Copilot CLI decrypted hidden commands and leaked local files The case Adversa AI got the GitHub Copilot CLI agent to decrypt hidden commands in ciphertext and obey them. The result was the exfiltration of local files from the machine in autopilot mode and without a visible confirmation step (Source: csoonline.com). GitHub validated the finding and rejected it as a vulnerability, and their reading is that the agent behaves as expected from a system that follows its context. This is uncomfortable, I know... the software did not break, an assumption broke, and it is the one that the agent tells apart the data it reads from the orders it receives.
articles.author: Sammi De Blas

articles.title: A School IT Teacher Watches a Student's Screen Without Touching It Using view-only mode for safe, hands-off observation
articles.excerpt: Mr. Joseph teaches computer science and also looks after the school's lab. A student calls out that her program has stopped working. Walking across the room is easy, but Mr. Joseph is helping three ot…
articles.body: Mr. Joseph teaches computer science and also looks after the school's lab. A student calls out that her program has stopped working. Walking across the room is easy, but Mr. Joseph is helping three other students at the same time, and he wants to see her screen before deciding whether the problem is quick or serious. He opens her lab PC from his own laptop using DeskVNC and switches on view-only mode. In this mode he can watch everything happening on her screen, but his mouse and keyboard do nothing there. That matters in a classroom. A stray click from the teacher's side could close her file, and the student would lose the habit of fixing her own mistakes. He sees the error message, notices that she has saved the file in the wrong folder and tells her what to check. She fixes it herself.

articles.body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR Apple built a flexible graphite pipe into the iPhone Duo hinge to dissipate excess heat between the two chassis halves when folded. Combined with an unstacked A20 Pro SoC and vapor chamber, the active thermal hinge helps maintain peak performance for longer under heavy loads. Android foldables have used graphite sheets as part of the display stack or on the chassis on either side of the spine, but have not typically used the spine itself for cooling. Foldables have spent years balancing thinner profiles with flagship-grade SoCs and the resulting thermal dilemma.

articles.title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Is a Near-Perfect Metroidvania
articles.excerpt: 'Castlevania: Belmont's Curse' lives up to this series' lofty legacy with outstanding platforming, world design, and ambiance.
articles.body: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse , the first mainline installment in over a decade, stabs this hypothetical through the heart, proving that Castlevania still has a lot more to give. By combining throwback appeal with razor-sharp gameplay built on the brilliant Dead Cells , Evil Empire’s latest lives up to Castlevania’s legendary status. From its bold use of color that makes the gothic visuals pop, to a new card-based Arcana system, Belmont’s Curse breathes new life into these games while honing in on what makes this series special. As good as many of Castlevania’s spiritual follow-ups have been, there’s something singular about facing the Lord of Darkness under a full moon to the tune of “Bloody Tears,” a reunion that feels like fate.
articles.author: Elijah Gonzalez

articles.title: Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse Review
articles.excerpt: A long-awaited return that brings the series into the modern era with a fast-paced focus on action first.
articles.body: Nearly two decades after the last mainline 2D Castlevania game,the team behind 2023’s Dead Cell’s Return to Castlevania DLC has been given the keys to Dracula’s Castle for real. Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse aims to breathe fresh life into this 40-year-old series with a creative blend of old and new ideas. With a brand new Belmont wielding the family whip, familiar foes in your way, and modern conveniences that have become expected in the genre, developer Evil Empire has largely hit their mark – but if you are a longtime fan expecting Belmont’s Curse to be a completely faithful revival of the series we played back in the early 2000s, then you will want to think again. This is a different breed of monster you're hunting, both for good and for ill.

articles.body: Two decades later, this spectacle from Battlestar Galactica season 3’s “Exodus, Part 2” remains unforgettable sci-fi TV. It’s dazzling and horrifying, and still one of the coolest things ever broadcast on science-fiction television. From a tactical standpoint, the “Adama Maneuver” is absolutely bonkers and one of the riskiest spaceship tactics, perhaps ever (sorry, Vice-Admiral Holdo). articles.body: SpaceX just broke an uncharacteristically long Starlink launch drought. The company sent 27 of its Starlink internet satellites to low Earth orbit (LEO) today (Oct. 12), launching them atop a Falcon 9 rocket from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base at 8:28 p.m. EDT (5:28 p.m. local time; 0028 GMT on Oct. 13) It was the first Starlink mission for a Falcon 9 since Sept. 19 , which was another 27-satellite liftoff from Vandenberg. For some perspective on this recent gap: Between Aug. 19 and Sept. 6, a span of 19 days, SpaceX launched seven Starlink missions with Falcon 9s. articles.title: Astronomers witness supermassive black hole gorge on a cosmic meal before 'burping' radio jets 300 days later
articles.excerpt: Using the NASA spacecraft Swift, astronomers observed a supermassive black hole burping radio jets 300 days after a heavy cosmic meal.
articles.body: Using the NASA X-ray spacecraft Swift combined with radio observations, astronomers have observed a supermassive black hole burping radio jets 300 days after a heavy cosmic meal. The team was also able to roughly estimate the mass of this feeding cosmic titan, which sits at the heart of the Perseus Cluster, a massive collection of thousands of galaxies. The black hole sits at the center of the galaxy NGC 1275, located around 225 light-years away, and is the brightest galaxy of the Perseus Cluster . The supermassive black hole first flared in X-rays, which indicated an increase in the rate at which it was accreting matter.

articles.title: The moon could turn astronauts into 'walking, high voltage capacitors' that accidentally zap spacecraft
articles.excerpt: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions.
articles.body: NASA is asking for ideas to stop static electricity from zapping astronauts or critical hardware during moon missions. The agency opened a "Lunar Grounding Challenge" to avoid situations where an astronaut on the moon could become "a walking, high voltage capacitor." Submissions for the $150,000 competition are due Jan. 15 and you can see the requirements here . NASA is hoping to put astronaut boots at the lunar south pole in 2028 during the Artemis 4 or 5 missions, on the first landing mission since NASA's Apollo 17 in 1972. But simulations suggest that both "tribocharging" (electric-charge transfer between two objects) and plasma charging (from ambient gas in the region) could build up electric charge on spacesuits.

articles.title: NASA’s SpaceX CRS-35 Mission to Launch Health Research
articles.excerpt: NASA experiments focused on human and plant health and drug-resistant organisms will travel to the International Space Station aboard SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency…
articles.body: NASA experiments focused on human and plant health and drug-resistant organisms will travel to the International Space Station aboard SpaceX’s 35th Commercial Resupply Services mission for the agency from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida, advancing research that benefits life on Earth and future exploration. This research supports astronaut health during long-duration missions through four investigations from the agency’s Biological and Physical Sciences division, including 3D models of the human brain, a crop disease study, a faster way to assess astronaut health, and an analysis of antibiotic-resistant bacteria aboard the space station.

articles.body: Friday, October 16, 2026 Can AI design new life forms? In 2025, Stanford University PhD student Samuel King came up with a preliminary answer when he used a generative AI model to propose genetic blueprints for microscopic viruses. It isn’t yet an example of AI-generated life, but that could be next. Join senior AI reporter James O’Donnell as he interviews King about his work, being named one of MIT Technology Review’s Innovators Under 35 and new ways of seeing biology.
